items.title: Compact Kähler and rational Hodge polarization conventions
items.statement:
Assume AC, the standing convention of this page: the analytic and cohomological suppliers invoked below assume full AC. A **Kähler manifold** is a complex manifold $X$ of complex dimension $n\ge1$ ([[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]) with a Hermitian metric $g$ whose real fundamental form $\omega(v,w)=g(Jv,w)$ is closed, $d\omega=0$, and positive, $\omega(v,Jv)>0$ for $v\ne0$; it is **compact Kähler** when $X$ is compact. The complex structure orients $X$, $(e_1,Je_1,\dots,e_n,Je_n)$ being positive for every complex frame. Normalize the metric so that in an oriented orthonormal real coframe $(e_1,f_1,\dots,e_n,f_n)$ one has $\omega=\sum_{j=1}^n e_j\wedge f_j$ and $dV=\omega^n/n!$. For $n=0$, $X$ is a finite set of points with its unique complex structure, all operators below are zero, and $dV$ is the counting measure.

Complex-valued differential forms use the complex-linear extension of the Hodge star of [[def-riemannian-hodge-star]] and the integral inner product $\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle=\int_X\alpha\wedge*\bar\beta$, complex-linear in the first variable. In holomorphic charts the complex-valued $k$-forms split as $\Omega^k(X;\mathbb C)=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}\Omega^{p,q}(X)$ and $d=\partial+\bar\partial$ with $\partial,\bar\partial$ of bidegree $(1,0)$ and $(0,1)$. Put $L=\omega\wedge$, let $\Lambda,\partial^*,\bar\partial^*,d^*$ be the formal adjoints of $L,\partial,\bar\partial,d$ ([[lem-formal-adjoints-of-differential-operators-exist-and-are-unique]]), and $\Delta_d=dd^*+d^*d$, $\Delta_\partial=\partial\partial^*+\partial^*\partial$, $\Delta_{\bar\partial}=\bar\partial\bar\partial^*+\bar\partial^*\bar\partial$; write $\epsilon(k)=(-1)^{k(k-1)/2}$.

A **rational pure Hodge structure of weight $k$** is a finite-dimensional $\mathbb Q$-vector space $V$ with $V_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}V^{p,q}$ and $\overline{V^{p,q}}=V^{q,p}$. Its **Weil operator** $C$ acts as $i^{p-q}$ on $V^{p,q}$. A **polarization** is a rational nondegenerate bilinear form $Q$ with $Q(y,x)=(-1)^kQ(x,y)$, with $Q(V^{p,q},V^{a,b})=0$ unless $(a,b)=(q,p)$, and with $h(x,y)=Q(Cx,\bar y)$ positive definite Hermitian. A **rational sub-Hodge structure** is a rational subspace $U$ with $U_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}(U_{\mathbb C}\cap V^{p,q})$, and the **Tate shift** $V(-r)$ keeps the underlying rational space with bidegrees $(p+r,q+r)$ and weight $k+2r$.
items.strategy: Definition and conventions, so no proof section. Well-definedness: the bidegree splitting and $d=\partial+\bar\partial$ are chart-local and glue because holomorphic chart transitions are complex-linear and preserve bidegree ([[def-bigraded-complex-differential-forms]], [[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]); the complex orientation is frame-independent because a complex change of basis has positive real determinant; the complex-linear star and the metric on exterior powers are [[def-riemannian-hodge-star]] and [[prop-riemannian-metrics-induce-metrics-on-dual-tensor-and-exterior-bundles]]; $\Lambda,\partial^*,\bar\partial^*,d^*$ exist uniquely by [[lem-formal-adjoints-of-differential-operators-exist-and-are-unique]]; every sum over $p,q$ is finite. AC: the definitional content is choice-free; the first sentence records the page-wide convention and declares [[def-axiom-of-choice]] so that the items invoking the analytic suppliers (whose statements assume AC) carry the assumption explicitly to their own consumers. Sources: Schnell classes 16-18 (operators $L,\Lambda,H$ for an orthonormal coframe, the star and the sign $\epsilon(k)$), Demailly VI §5.1-5.2 (complex Hodge star, $d=d'+d''$, adjoint operators, $L$ and $\Lambda=\star^{-1}L\star$), Deligne II (2.1.10)-(2.1.17) (Hodge structures of weight $n$, the Tate twist, polarizations) and (2.1.14) (the orientation $\mathrm{or}_i(X)$ of a complex manifold). The source-review caveat that the class-17 two-plane table contains typographical slips is recorded on the pointwise Lefschetz item, not here.
items.axiom_use: None in the definitional content. The declared [[def-axiom-of-choice]] records the page-wide convention that the analytic and cohomological suppliers of the later items assume full AC; each such item declares its own use.

items.title: Rational cohomology scalar comparison on compact smooth manifolds
items.statement: Assume AC. For a compact smooth manifold $X$, the natural coefficient maps induce isomorphisms $H^k(X;\mathbb Q)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}F\cong H^k(X;F)$ for every characteristic-zero field $F$, finite-dimensional in each degree. For $F=\mathbb R,\mathbb C$ these identify singular cohomology with the real or complex de Rham cohomology. They preserve cup products and are natural for maps between such manifolds. No ordered-field or positivity structure is asserted for a general $F$.
items.strategy: Use the finite CW homotopy model of $X$ ([[lem-compact-smooth-manifolds-have-finite-cw-models-under-countable-choice]], stated under AC_ω, derived here from AC by [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]) to get finite-dimensional $H_k(X;\mathbb Q)$ and finite generation of all $H_k(X;\mathbb Z)$; [[thm-cellular-homology-computes-singular-homology]] converts the model into singular homology without extra choice. Step 1: choose, using full AC, direct complements $Z_k=B_k\oplus A_k$ and $C_k=Z_k\oplus T_k$ in the singular rational chain complex; the boundary bijects $T_k$ onto $B_{k-1}$, and tensoring with a characteristic-zero field $F$ preserves the splittings and the bijection, so $H_k(X;F)=H_k(X;\mathbb Q)\otimes F$ via the canonical coefficient map (checked on cycles). Step 2: the field universal coefficient theorem ([[thm-universal-coefficient-theorem-for-cohomology-over-a-pid]]) has $\operatorname{Ext}^1_F=0$, so evaluation is a canonical isomorphism $H^k(X;F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_F(H_k(X;F),F)$; with finite-dimensional $H_k(X;\mathbb Q)$ the natural map $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Q}(H_k(X;\mathbb Q),\mathbb Q)\otimes F\to\operatorname{Hom}_F(H_k(X;\mathbb Q)\otimes F,F)$ is an isomorphism (it is the identity on a finite basis), identifying $H^k(X;\mathbb Q)\otimes F$ with $H^k(X;F)$. Cup products commute with coefficient inclusion by the front/back formula and the construction is natural by precomposition on cochains. Step 3: for $F=\mathbb R$ the identification with de Rham cohomology is [[thm-de-rham-theorem]]; complex forms split uniquely into real and imaginary parts, so kernels, images and quotients complexify, giving $F=\mathbb C$. The strategy explicitly avoids choosing bases of infinite-dimensional spaces outside Step 1, so the only full-AC step is the complement decomposition there.
items.axiom_use: Full AC: direct-complement choices in the singular rational chain complex in Step 1. Its countable consequences are used through the finite-CW-model lemma, the de Rham theorem and the universal coefficient theorem; [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]] supplies AC_ω from AC. The construction is not choice-free.

items.title: Top de Rham integration equals fundamental-class evaluation
items.statement: Assume AC. For a compact oriented smooth boundaryless $m$-manifold $M$ and a smooth real or complex top form $\alpha$, the natural de Rham comparison satisfies $\langle J_M[\alpha],[M]\rangle=\int_M\alpha$. Thus rational cup products that become top de Rham forms integrate to their rational fundamental-class evaluation.
items.strategy: Use the de Rham comparison $J_M$ of [[thm-de-rham-theorem]] as the composition of integration of forms over smooth simplices with the inverse of smooth-to-continuous singular restriction. Step 1: fix a smooth singular cycle $z=\sum_{j=1}^Na_j\sigma_j$ representing the fundamental class $[M]$ ([[thm-smooth-singular-chains-compute-singular-homology]], [[def-fundamental-class-of-a-compact-oriented-manifold]]), so $\langle J_M[\alpha],[M]\rangle=\sum_j a_j\int_{\Delta^m}\sigma_j^*\alpha$ by the defining integration cocycle. Step 2: extend each $\sigma_j$ smoothly near its simplex and apply Sard in coordinate charts ([[thm-morse-sard-for-euclidean-maps]]); critical values together with the images of the $(m-1)$-dimensional faces form a null set, a finite union of null sets remaining null. Outside it each preimage of $y\in M$ is interior and regular, and there are finitely many: an infinite set would have an accumulation point by compactness, which can lie neither on a face nor at a regular point. Excising disjoint inverse-image balls ([[thm-excision-for-singular-homology]]) and using the local-orientation characterization of the fundamental class identifies the weighted multiplicity $\sum_j a_j\sum_{x\in\sigma_j^{-1}(y)}\operatorname{sgn}\det D\sigma_j(x)$ with $1$ at every such $y$. Step 3: on the regular locus choose a countable locally finite partition subordinate to precompact inverse-function neighbourhoods, apply the oriented change of variables ([[thm-change-of-variables-for-oriented-manifold-diffeomorphisms]]) on each injective chart, and use monotone convergence ([[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]]) on the pullback of the absolute density to justify summing the absolutely convergent integrals; the critical set contributes zero because its pulled-back top form has vanishing Jacobian and the faces have measure zero. Hence $\sum_j a_j\int_{\sigma_j}\sigma_j^*\alpha=\int_M\alpha$. Real and imaginary parts give complex $\alpha$, and cup compatibility of $J_M$ gives the last sentence. The dimension-zero case is the finite signed point sum and is handled directly. The proof consumes only AC_ω; full AC is recorded as the page convention and AC_ω is obtained from it by [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]].
items.axiom_use: Full AC as the page convention; the argument consumes only AC_ω, through smooth-singular comparison, the de Rham theorem and smooth partitions of unity. [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]] supplies AC_ω. Sard, change of variables, excision and monotone convergence are choice-free.

items.title: Hermitian exterior Lefschetz decomposition and Weil star identity
items.statement: Let $V$ be a real vector space of dimension $2n$ with a positive-definite inner product $g$, a compatible complex structure $J$ ($g(Jv,Jw)=g(v,w)$, $J^2=-1$), fundamental form $\omega(v,w)=g(Jv,w)$ and the orientation in which $(e_1,Je_1,\dots,e_n,Je_n)$ is positive, with the conventions of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]]. On the complexified exterior algebra $\Lambda^\bullet V_{\mathbb C}$ the operators $L=\omega\wedge$, $\Lambda=L^*$ and $H=[L,\Lambda]$ satisfy $[L,\Lambda]=H$, $H|_{\Lambda^k}=(k-n)I$, $[H,L]=2L$ and $[H,\Lambda]=-2\Lambda$. Every degree-$k$ element has a unique decomposition $\sum_{r\ge\max(0,k-n)}L^ru_r$ with $\Lambda u_r=0$ and $\deg u_r=k-2r$. For primitive $u$ of degree $t$, $L^{n-t+1}u=0$ and $$\Lambda^sL^ru=\frac{r!}{(r-s)!}\frac{(n-t-r+s)!}{(n-t-r)!}L^{r-s}u\qquad(0\le s\le r\le n-t);$$ no nonzero primitive element has $t>n$. Hence $L^{n-k}:\Lambda^k\to\Lambda^{2n-k}$ is an isomorphism for $k\le n$, and primitive degree $k$ is equivalently $L^{n-k+1}u=0$. With $J=i^{p-q}$ on type $(p,q)$ and $W=\exp L\exp(-\Lambda)\exp L$ one has $W|_{\Lambda^k}=\epsilon(k)J*$; in particular, if $u$ is primitive of type $(p,q)$ and $k=p+q$, then $$*u=\frac{\epsilon(k)i^{q-p}}{(n-k)!}L^{n-k}u.$$ All decomposition projections are rational polynomials in $L,\Lambda$ on each fixed degree.
items.strategy: Pointwise Hermitian linear algebra; in-run dependencies are the conventions item and the published Hodge-star items. Sources: Schnell class 16 (Lemma 16.1, Propositions 16.2 and 16.4), Schnell class 17 (Lefschetz decomposition, Lemma 17.1, Proposition 17.3 with its two-plane induction), Demailly VI §5.2-5.3 ((5.9)-(5.17)). Step 1: on an oriented orthonormal two-plane $e,f$ with $Je=f$, $L$ sends $1$ to $e\wedge f$ and kills $e,f$, while $\Lambda=L^*$ sends $e\wedge f$ to $1$ and kills $e,f$; hence $[L,\Lambda]$ has eigenvalues $-1,0,0,1$ in degrees $0,1,1,2$. Summing over orthogonal two-planes (distinct factors commute) gives $[L,\Lambda]=H$, $H|_{\Lambda^k}=(k-n)I$ and the other two relations. Repeated commutation of $\Lambda$ through $L$ gives $\Lambda L^ru=r(n-t-r+1)L^{r-1}u$ for primitive $u$ of degree $t$; iterating gives the displayed coefficient formula and the norm identity $\|L^ru\|^2=r(n-t-r+1)\|L^{r-1}u\|^2$, whose positivity through $r=n-t$ and vanishing at $r=n-t+1$ shows the string is nonzero exactly for $0\le r\le n-t$ and that no nonzero primitive has $t>n$. Step 2: $\ker\Lambda=(\operatorname{im}L)^\perp$ in each degree; subtracting from a vector the top $\Lambda$-power of a multiple of $L$ iteratively splits it as $\sum L^ru_r$ with $\Lambda u_r=0$, and applying $\Lambda^s$ at the largest surviving index to a vanishing sum gives uniqueness and the rational-polynomial projectors (choose the highest lowering power, divide by its displayed nonzero integer coefficient, repeat). The string computation gives $L^{n-k}:\Lambda^k\to\Lambda^{2n-k}$ invertible for $k\le n$ and $\Lambda u=0\iff L^{n-k+1}u=0$. Step 3: $W=\exp L\exp(-\Lambda)\exp L$ satisfies $W=\epsilon(k)J*$ on $\Lambda^k$ by two-plane induction: on a two-plane multiplication of the three exponentials gives $W(1)=e\wedge f$, $W(e)=e$, $W(f)=f$, $W(e\wedge f)=-1$, matching $\epsilon(\deg)J*$; both sides multiply over wedges of orthogonal even-dimensional factors with $*(a\wedge b)=(-1)^{\deg a\deg b}(*a)\wedge(*b)$ and $\epsilon(a+b)=(-1)^{\deg a\deg b}\epsilon(a)\epsilon(b)$. Step 4: model a primitive string of length $m=n-k$ by $L^ru/r!\leftrightarrow\binom mrx^{m-r}y^r$ so that $L=y\partial_x$ and $\Lambda=x\partial_y$; the three exponentials compose to the substitution $x\mapsto y$, $y\mapsto-x$, hence $Wu=L^mu/m!$, and $J$ is the constant $i^{q-p}$ along the string, giving $*u=\epsilon(k)i^{q-p}L^mu/m!$. Source-review warning retained: Schnell's class-17 two-plane table has typographical slips (a duplicated $J*e_2$ entry and a $k\le0$ range); the signs above are re-derived from the star characterization of [[def-hodge-star-on-an-oriented-inner-product-space]] and must be re-checked independently rather than copied.
items.axiom_use: None: finite-dimensional real exterior algebra with canonical orthogonal decompositions and integer coefficients; no basis or complement is chosen from an infinite family.

items.title: Kähler commutators and preservation of harmonic types
items.statement: Assume AC. On a Kähler manifold, with the conventions of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]], the formal adjoints satisfy $$[\Lambda,\partial]=i\bar\partial^*,\qquad[\Lambda,\bar\partial]=-i\partial^*,\qquad[\bar\partial^*,L]=i\partial,\qquad[\partial^*,L]=-i\bar\partial.$$ One has $\Delta_d=2\Delta_\partial=2\Delta_{\bar\partial}$, the mixed anticommutators $\partial\bar\partial^*+\bar\partial^*\partial$ and $\bar\partial\partial^*+\partial^*\bar\partial$ vanish, and $\Delta_d$ commutes with $L,\Lambda,\partial,\bar\partial,*$ and preserves each $(p,q)$ type.
items.strategy: Sources: Schnell classes 17-18 (proof of the Kähler identities; Corollaries 18.1-18.2), Demailly VI §6.1 ((6.3)-(6.7)). Step 1 (normal coordinates): at $x_0$ choose holomorphic coordinates with $g(0)=I$; closedness $d\omega=0$ is equivalent to $\partial_ah_{b\bar c}(0)=\partial_bh_{a\bar c}(0)$, and the quadratic holomorphic change $z_b=w_b-\tfrac12\sum_{a,c}\partial_ah_{c\bar b}(0)w_aw_c$ (indices identified by $h(0)$) is invertible near $0$ by [[thm-holomorphic-inverse-function-theorem-several-variables]] and makes $h'(w)=I+O(|w|^2)$; hence the metric, inverse metric and volume coefficients have vanishing first derivatives at the point, and integration by parts against the Euclidean density ([[thm-general-stokes-theorem]] localized to charts) gives the flat formal-adjoint formulas there. Step 2 (commutators): in a unitary coframe with $\omega=i\sum a_jb_j$, $a_j=dz_j\wedge$, $b_j=d\bar z_j\wedge$, $|dz_j|=1$, the wedge and contraction operators obey $a_j^*a_l+a_la_j^*=\delta_{jl}$ and its barred analogue with all mixed anticommutators zero; at the normal point $\partial=\sum a_j\partial_{z_j}$, $\bar\partial=\sum b_j\partial_{\bar z_j}$, $\partial^*=-\sum a_j^*\partial_{\bar z_j}$, $\bar\partial^*=-\sum b_j^*\partial_{z_j}$, $L=i\sum a_jb_j$, $\Lambda=-i\sum b_j^*a_j^*$; the anticommutation relations give $[\Lambda,a_j]=-ib_j^*$ and $[\Lambda,b_j]=ia_j^*$, hence the first two identities, and adjunction gives the other two. Normalization caveat: this computation uses Demailly's normalization $\omega=i\sum dz_j\wedge d\bar z_j$ with $|dz_j|=1$, while [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]] normalizes $\omega=\sum e_j\wedge f_j$ with $e_j,f_j$ orthonormal (so $dz_j=e_j+if_j$, $|dz_j|^2=2$ and $L=\frac i2\sum(dz_j\wedge)(d\bar z_j\wedge)$); the four identities are invariant under a constant rescaling $g\mapsto\lambda g$ ($L\mapsto\lambda L$, $\Lambda\mapsto\lambda^{-1}\Lambda$, $\partial^*,\bar\partial^*\mapsto\lambda^{-1}\partial^*,\lambda^{-1}\bar\partial^*$), so they hold in either normalization, but the author must not mix the two normalizations in one computation. All operators are first order with coefficients built from first derivatives of the metric, so equality at every normal point gives the global identities. Step 3 (Laplacians and mixed anticommutators): use graded brackets, for which the bracket of two odd operators is the anticommutator. From $\bar\partial^*=-i[\Lambda,\partial]$ the expansion of $[\partial,[\Lambda,\partial]]$ has its two middle $\partial\Lambda\partial$ terms cancel and the remaining terms contain $\partial^2$, so $[\partial,\bar\partial^*]=0$; adjunction gives $[\bar\partial,\partial^*]=0$. Graded Jacobi gives $[\bar\partial,[\Lambda,\partial]]=[\partial,[\bar\partial,\Lambda]]$, and with $[\bar\partial,\Lambda]=i\partial^*$ this yields $[\bar\partial,\bar\partial^*]=[\partial,\partial^*]$; expanding $(\partial+\bar\partial)(\partial^*+\bar\partial^*)+(\partial^*+\bar\partial^*)(\partial+\bar\partial)$ gives $\Delta_d=2\Delta_\partial=2\Delta_{\bar\partial}$. Step 4 (commutation and types): $d\omega=0$ gives $[\partial,L]=[\bar\partial,L]=0$, hence $[\Delta_\partial,L]=[\partial,[\partial^*,L]]=-i[\partial,\bar\partial]=0$ and by adjunction $[\Delta_\partial,\Lambda]=0$; commutation with $\partial,\bar\partial$ follows from their squares and $\Delta_d=2\Delta_\partial=2\Delta_{\bar\partial}$; on the even-dimensional complexified forms $d^*=-*d*$ and $*^2=(-1)^k$ in degree $k$ give $[\Delta_d,*]=0$; $\Delta_{\bar\partial}=\Delta_d/2$ has bidegree $(0,0)$, so $\Delta_d$ preserves each $\Omega^{p,q}$.
items.axiom_use: Full AC is stated as the page convention and declared via [[def-axiom-of-choice]]; the argument itself consumes only AC_ω, through the general Stokes theorem, and AC_ω is obtained from AC by [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]. The normal-coordinate and commutator computations are choice-free.

items.title: Compact Kähler Hodge decomposition from elliptic harmonic forms
items.statement: Assume AC. For a compact Kähler manifold $X$ in the sense of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]], every de Rham class has a unique smooth harmonic representative and $$H^k(X;\mathbb C)=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}H^{p,q}(X),\qquad \overline{H^{p,q}(X)}=H^{q,p}(X).$$ Here $H^{p,q}(X)$ is precisely the set of classes with a $d$-closed smooth representative of type $(p,q)$, so the decomposition is independent of the Kähler metric. Writing $\Omega_X^p$ for the sheaf of holomorphic $p$-forms (the kernel of $\bar\partial$ on the sheaf $\mathcal A^{p,0}$ of smooth $(p,0)$-forms), $H^{p,q}(X)$ is isomorphic to $H^q(X,\Omega_X^p)$, the sheaf cohomology of [[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]. The Hodge filtration $F^a=\bigoplus_{p\ge a}H^{p,k-p}$ of $H^k(X;\mathbb C)$ equals the filtration induced by the holomorphic-degree filtration of the de Rham complex, whose spectral sequence has $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(X,\Omega_X^p)$ and degenerates at $E_1$. Pullback by holomorphic maps of compact Kähler manifolds and cup product preserve Hodge type, so $H^k(X;\mathbb Q)$ is a functorial rational pure Hodge structure.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Step 1 (harmonic representatives): $\Delta_d=dd^*+d^*d$ has principal symbol $|\xi|^2$ and nonnegative energy $\|du\|^2+\|d^*u\|^2$; [[thm-sobolev-compactness-and-elliptic-estimates-give-fredholm-hodge-decomposition]] gives finite-dimensional smooth kernel $\mathcal H$, smoothing orthogonal projection $\Pi$ and Green inverse $G$ with $u=\Pi u+\Delta_dGu$. For closed $u$, $dGu$ is harmonic and exact, hence orthogonal to harmonic forms by Stokes and zero, so $u=\Pi u+dd^*Gu$; a harmonic exact form vanishes, giving uniqueness. Complex dimension zero is handled separately as a finite discrete set. Step 2 (type decomposition): [[lem-kahler-commutators-and-laplacian-type-preservation]] gives $\Delta_d=2\Delta_{\bar\partial}$, so $\Pi$ preserves bidegree and the decomposition of $H^k(X;\mathbb C)$ into the $H^{p,q}(X)$ follows by taking type components of the unique harmonic representative, with conjugation exchanging $H^{p,q}$ and $H^{q,p}$. Metric independence, holomorphic pullback compatibility and cup compatibility hold because type and closedness are local and the de Rham comparison identifies wedge with cup; [[lem-rational-cohomology-scalar-comparison-for-compact-smooth-manifolds]] supplies the rational structure and the real and complex comparisons. Step 3 (sheaf comparison): for fixed type the same elliptic supplier applies to $\Delta_{\bar\partial}=\Delta_d/2$, so harmonic $(p,q)$-forms represent the global Dolbeault cohomology. The polydisc lemma ([[thm-dolbeault-lemma-polydisc]]) gives stalkwise exactness of $0\to\Omega_X^p\to\mathcal A^{p,0}\to\cdots\to\mathcal A^{p,n}\to0$, where $\Omega_X^p$ is the kernel of $\bar\partial$ (its sections are exactly the holomorphic $p$-forms, since $\bar\partial f=0$ in degree zero is the holomorphic coefficient condition); each $\mathcal A^{p,q}$ is a sheaf of modules over the smooth functions (restriction of scalars from complex to real-valued smooth functions), hence acyclic by [[thm-smooth-function-module-sheaves-are-acyclic]]; [[thm-acyclic-resolution-theorem-for-right-derived-functors]] (which assumes DC, obtained from AC by [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]) identifies $H^q(X,\Omega_X^p)$ with that global Dolbeault cohomology, hence with the harmonic $(p,q)$-forms. Step 4 (Hodge filtration, $E_1$ degeneration): filter the global de Rham complex by holomorphic degree and reindex (chain degree $-k$, filtration index $-a$) so that [[thm-bounded-filtered-complex-spectral-sequence-abuts-to-filtered-homology]] applies; the filtration is finite in each degree because $X$ is compact of complex dimension $n$. Its first page is $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(X,\Omega_X^p)$ by Step 3 and $d_1$ is induced by $\partial$ on $\bar\partial$-closed representatives; every $E_1$ class has a $d$-closed harmonic representative, so $d_1=0$. Since all $E_r^{p,q}$ are finite dimensional and $E_\infty^{p,q}$ is a subquotient of $E_1^{p,q}$, while the abutment gives $\sum_{p+q=k}\dim E_\infty^{p,q}=\dim H^k(X;\mathbb C)=\sum_{p+q=k}\dim H^{p,q}(X)=\sum_{p+q=k}\dim E_1^{p,q}$ by Steps 2-3, all these dimensions are equal; hence every differential vanishes and $E_1=E_2=\cdots=E_\infty$, and then $F^a(H^k)=\bigoplus_{p\ge a}H^{p,k-p}$, which is the stated filtration equality. Functoriality for holomorphic maps is pullback of forms, which preserves bidegree and closedness.
items.axiom_use: Full AC: declared dependency, used through the compact elliptic/Fredholm supplier ([[thm-sobolev-compactness-and-elliptic-estimates-give-fredholm-hodge-decomposition]]), the polydisc Dolbeault lemma and the smooth-function acyclicity theorem, all of which assume AC; the acyclic-resolution theorem assumes DC, supplied by [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]. The sheaf-cohomology definition also assumes AC. No stronger principle and no choice in the subsequent linear algebra.

items.title: Hodge decomposition and polarization of a point
items.statement: Assume AC. The one-point space is a compact Kähler manifold of complex dimension zero in the sense of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]]. Its rational cohomology is $H^0(\mathrm{pt};\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$ with the single Hodge type $(0,0)$, all higher cohomology vanishes, and $Q(x,y)=xy$ is a rational polarization. The hard-Lefschetz map $L^0$ in degree zero is the identity.
items.strategy: Direct computation in the dimension-zero conventions of the definition, using the page's theorem and rational scalar comparison for the rational structure. Step 1: on a point the complexified form complex is $\mathbb C$ in degree zero with zero differential and no forms in positive degrees, so $H^0(\mathrm{pt};\mathbb C)=\mathbb C$ is purely of type $(0,0)$, $H^k=0$ for $k>0$, and the unique harmonic representative of the degree-zero class is the constant function; the theorem's decomposition and the conjugation statement are then identities. Step 2: [[lem-rational-cohomology-scalar-comparison-for-compact-smooth-manifolds]] identifies $H^0(\mathrm{pt};\mathbb Q)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C$ with $H^0(\mathrm{pt};\mathbb C)=\mathbb C$, so $H^0(\mathrm{pt};\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q$ is the rational structure of the type-$(0,0)$ piece. The operators $L=\omega\wedge$ and $\Lambda$ vanish because $\omega=0$, so the degree-zero hard-Lefschetz map $L^0$ is the identity. Step 3: $Q(x,y)=xy$ on $\mathbb Q$ is nondegenerate, symmetric of weight-zero parity, has no off-diagonal type pairings to check, and $h(x,y)=Q(Cx,\bar y)=x\bar y$ is positive definite Hermitian for $C=I$, so it is a rational polarization. The example consumes AC only through the theorem and the comparison lemma; the point computations themselves are choice-free.
items.axiom_use: Full AC inherited from the page's compact-Kähler theorem and the rational scalar comparison lemma; declared via [[def-axiom-of-choice]]. The direct computations on the one-point space use no choice.
